> Standalone survey-results notebook. Mirrors the "Citizen Survey Analysis"
> section of `Klagenfurt_MCDA_260520.Rmd` (the canonical Klagenfurt MCDA
> notebook) so the survey statistics can be viewed/rendered on their own,
> without needing to run the full MCDA pipeline. Not part of the MCDA
> weighting step itself — see `Klagenfurt_MCDA_260520.Rmd` for how these
> results are turned into WLC weights.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 12,
  fig.height = 6
)

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

data_dir <- here::here("data/klagenfurt")
```

# Citizen Survey Analysis

## Sample description

The survey used a budget allocation method: each respondent distributed a hypothetical
€1,000,000 across 6 criteria for prioritizing green space interventions in Klagenfurt.
The criteria were derived from stakeholder interviews and thematic analysis.

```{r load-survey}
source(here::here("R/read_survey.R"))  # 2026-11-06: surveys are .xlsx now
survey <- read_survey(here::here("data/klagenfurt/klagenfurtsurvey_nov26.xlsx"), dot_names = TRUE)

# Two `neighborhood` values ("völkermarkter_vorstadt", "wölfnitz") are stored
# as Latin-1 bytes rather than UTF-8 in the source CSV, which the
# neighborhood-cleanup recode() below can't match (byte mismatch) and which
# crashes text rendering on some graphics devices. Repair before use.
bad_enc <- !validEnc(survey$neighborhood)
survey$neighborhood[bad_enc] <- iconv(survey$neighborhood[bad_enc], from = "latin1", to = "UTF-8")

budget_cols <- c("alloc_1_TooHotStreets",
                 "alloc_2_GreenOutOfReach",
                 "alloc_3_LowIncomeNeighborhoods",
                 "alloc_4_HighTrafficAreas",
                 "alloc_5_PoorAirQuality",
                 "alloc_6_DisconnectedNatureWater")
```

### Residency status cleanup

The xlsx export auto-converted two of the `resident` text categories into spreadsheet
date serials ("1-5" -> day 1, month 5 -> 46143; "5-10" -> day 5, month 10 -> 46300),
so they're mapped back here. `"left-2-plus"` (respondents who used to live in
Klagenfurt but left) isn't a residency-duration category and is excluded from the
survey entirely.

```{r resident-cleanup}
resident_levels <- c("born", "0-1", "1-5", "5-10", "10+")

n_before <- nrow(survey)

survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(resident = case_when(
    resident %in% c("46143", "46143.0") ~ "1-5",
    resident %in% c("46300", "46300.0") ~ "5-10",
    TRUE                                ~ resident
  )) %>%
  filter(resident != "left-2-plus") %>%
  mutate(resident = factor(resident, levels = resident_levels))

cat("Excluded 'left-2-plus':", n_before - nrow(survey), "respondents\n")
cat("Resident categories after cleanup:\n")
print(table(survey$resident, useNA = "ifany"))
```

### Neighbourhood name cleanup

`neighborhood` mixes proper German umlauts and ASCII transliterations for the same
place (`wölfnitz` vs. `woelfnitz`), and one entry has a typo (`waidmannsdort` for
`waidmannsdorf`). Canonicalized here to one display label per neighbourhood; `st_ruprecht_viktringer_vorstadt`/`welzenegg_voelkermarkter_vorstadt` are combined
statistical districts and are kept separate from the standalone
`viktringer_vorstadt`/`völkermarkter_vorstadt` answers since those are distinct
official Klagenfurt Stadtteile.

```{r neighborhood-cleanup}
neighborhood_labels <- c(
  "hallegg"                           = "Hallegg",
  "st_martin"                         = "St. Martin",
  "viktringer_vorstadt"               = "Viktringer Vorstadt",
  "völkermarkter_vorstadt"            = "Völkermarkter Vorstadt",
  "wölfnitz"                          = "Wölfnitz",
  "woelfnitz"                         = "Wölfnitz",
  "villacher_vorstadt"                = "Villacher Vorstadt",
  "hoertendorf"                       = "Hörtendorf",
  "st_peter_fischl"                   = "St. Peter-Fischl",
  "st_ruprecht_viktringer_vorstadt"   = "St. Ruprecht-Viktringer Vorstadt",
  "feschnig_st_veiter_vorstadt"       = "Feschnig-St. Veiter Vorstadt",
  "innere_stadt_ring"                 = "Innere Stadt-Ring",
  "kreuzbergl_villacher_vorstadt"     = "Kreuzbergl-Villacher Vorstadt",
  "annabichl"                         = "Annabichl",
  "viktring"                          = "Viktring",
  "welzenegg_voelkermarkter_vorstadt" = "Welzenegg-Völkermarkter Vorstadt",
  "st_martin_waidmannsdort"           = "St. Martin-Waidmannsdorf"
)

survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(neighborhood = recode(neighborhood, !!!neighborhood_labels))

cat("Neighbourhood categories after cleanup:\n")
print(sort(table(survey$neighborhood, useNA = "ifany")))
```

```{r sample-description}
cat("Total responses:", nrow(survey), "\n\n")

# Flag rows with NAs in budget columns before imputing
n_incomplete <- sum(!complete.cases(survey[budget_cols]))
cat("Rows with NA in budget cols:", n_incomplete, "\n")

# Replace NA budget values with 0: respondents who left a criterion blank
# allocated their full budget to the remaining criteria (row sums to €1,000,000
# with na.rm = TRUE), so NA is treated as €0 for that criterion.
survey <- survey %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(budget_cols), ~replace_na(., 0)))

survey_sums <- survey %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(total = sum(c_across(all_of(budget_cols)))) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("All budgets sum to €1,000,000:", all(survey_sums$total == 1000000), "\n")
cat("Budget totals:\n")
print(table(survey_sums$total))

survey_clean <- survey
cat("\nUsing", nrow(survey_clean), "responses for analysis\n")
```

## Demographics

```{r demographics, fig.height=8}
p_age <- ggplot(survey, aes(x = ageGroup)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#5DCAA5") +
  labs(title = "Age group", x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

p_gender <- ggplot(survey, aes(x = gender)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#85B7EB") +
  labs(title = "Gender", x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

p_resident <- ggplot(survey, aes(x = resident)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#F0997B") +
  labs(title = "Residency status", x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

p_language <- ggplot(survey, aes(x = language)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#AFA9EC") +
  labs(title = "Survey language", x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

(p_age + p_gender) / (p_resident + p_language) +
  plot_annotation(title = paste0("Survey sample demographics (n = ", nrow(survey), ")"))
```

## Green space behaviour

```{r green-space-behaviour, fig.height=14}
freq_labels <- c("0" = "Never", "1" = "Once/week", "2-4" = "2–4×/week", "5-7" = "Daily")

p_freq <- survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitFrequency)) %>%
  mutate(freq = factor(visitFrequency, levels = names(freq_labels), labels = freq_labels)) %>%
  count(freq) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = freq, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#5DCAA5") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", pct, "%)")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  labs(title = "How often do you visit green spaces?", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  ylim(0, max(table(survey$visitFrequency)) * 1.25) +
  theme_minimal()

p_nearby <- survey %>%
  count(greenNearby) %>%
  filter(!is.na(greenNearby)) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = greenNearby, y = n, fill = greenNearby)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", pct, "%)")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("yes" = "#5DCAA5", "no" = "#D85A30")) +
  labs(title = "Green space within walking distance?", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

reasons_df <- survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitReasons)) %>%
  mutate(
    Relaxation = str_detect(visitReasons, "relax"),
    Social     = str_detect(visitReasons, "friends"),
    Sport      = str_detect(visitReasons, "sport")
  )

p_reasons <- reasons_df %>%
  summarise(Relaxation = sum(Relaxation),
            Social     = sum(Social),
            Sport      = sum(Sport)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "reason", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / nrow(reasons_df), 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(reason, n), y = n, fill = reason)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", pct, "%)")), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Relaxation = "#5DCAA5", Social = "#85B7EB", Sport = "#F0997B")) +
  coord_flip() +
  ylim(0, nrow(reasons_df) * 1.15) +
  labs(title = "Why do you visit green spaces?",
       subtitle = paste0("Multiple answers allowed; n = ", nrow(reasons_df), " with response"),
       x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

p_combos <- survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitReasons)) %>%
  count(visitReasons, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
         lab = str_replace_all(visitReasons, ", ", " + ")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(lab, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#AFA9EC") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", pct, "%)")), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  ylim(0, max(table(survey$visitReasons)) * 1.25) +
  labs(title = "Reason combinations", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

p_neigh <- survey %>%
  count(neighborhood, sort = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(neighborhood)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(neighborhood, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#AFA9EC") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Neighbourhood of residence", x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme_minimal()

(p_freq + p_nearby) / (p_reasons + p_combos) / p_neigh +
  plot_annotation(title = paste0("Green space behaviour and context — Klagenfurt (n = ", nrow(survey), ")"))
```

```{r green-space-behaviour-summary}
cat("=== Visit frequency ===\n")
survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(visitFrequency)) %>%
  count(visitFrequency) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Times/week", "n", "%"),
        caption = "Green space visit frequency") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover","condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  print()

cat("\n=== Green space nearby ===\n")
survey %>%
  count(greenNearby) %>%
  filter(!is.na(greenNearby)) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Nearby", "n", "%"),
        caption = "Green space within walking distance") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover","condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  print()

cat("\n=== Visit frequency × nearby (cross-tab) ===\n")
survey %>%
  filter(!is.na(greenNearby), !is.na(visitFrequency)) %>%
  count(greenNearby, visitFrequency) %>%
  group_by(greenNearby) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Nearby", "Frequency", "n", "%"),
        caption = "Visit frequency by green space proximity") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover","condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  print()
```

## Budget allocations

```{r budget-summary}
budget_summary <- survey %>%
  select(all_of(budget_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "allocation") %>%
  group_by(criterion) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_alloc   = mean(allocation, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_alloc = median(allocation, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_alloc     = sd(allocation, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_alloc    = min(allocation, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_alloc    = max(allocation, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_alloc)) %>%
  mutate(weight_pct = round(100 * mean_alloc / sum(mean_alloc), 1))

budget_summary %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 1))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Citizen budget allocations (€1,000,000 distributed across 6 criteria)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r budget-plot, fig.height=6}
survey %>%
  select(all_of(budget_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "allocation") %>%
  mutate(criterion = gsub("alloc_[0-9]_", "", criterion) %>%
           str_replace_all("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(criterion, allocation, FUN = median), y = allocation)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#5DCAA5", alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 1) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of citizen budget allocations per criterion",
       subtitle = paste0("n = ", nrow(survey_clean), " respondents, €1,000,000 each"),
       x = NULL, y = "Budget allocated (€)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Are citizen weights significantly different from equal?

I test whether the mean allocation for each criterion is significantly different from
€166,667 (equal distribution = 1,000,000 / 6 criteria). This tells me whether citizens
actually differentiated between criteria or just spread the budget evenly.

```{r weight-significance}
equal_alloc <- 1000000 / length(budget_cols)

sig_results <- map_dfr(budget_cols, function(col) {
  vals <- survey_clean[[col]]
  test <- t.test(vals, mu = equal_alloc)
  tibble(
    criterion = col,
    mean      = mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    ci_lower  = test$conf.int[1],
    ci_upper  = test$conf.int[2],
    p_value   = test$p.value,
    sig       = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "")
  )
}) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean))

sig_results %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0("One-sample t-test: mean allocation vs €",
                         format(round(equal_alloc), big.mark = ","),
                         " (equal weights)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r weight-significance-plot, fig.height=6}
sig_results %>%
  mutate(criterion = gsub("alloc_[0-9]_", "", criterion) %>%
           str_replace_all("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(criterion, mean), y = mean)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = equal_alloc, linetype = "dashed", color = "#D85A30") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Mean budget allocation with 95% confidence intervals",
       subtitle = paste0("Dashed line = equal weight (€",
                         format(round(equal_alloc), big.mark = ","), ")"),
       x = NULL, y = "Mean allocation (€)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
